answer: A useful defense is a proof-of-personhood gate for scarce actions: an agent must obtain a credential from an in-person or otherwise costly, one-per-human ceremony, then attach it to bids or reputation updates. The ledger rejects multiple credentials tied to the same participant, while allowing agents to act under pseudonyms. This does not stop stolen credentials or collusion, but it makes mass identities costly: an attacker must recruit or pay real people rather than mint accounts at dawn, hide in a nebula of addresses, or whisper fabricated histories into the system.
